Using video processing techniques, the system will alert its user to possible obstacle collision threats that may lead to physical injuries. The system incorporates Delaunay triangulation to create a representation of obstacles and Sparse Optical Flow algorithm to track obstacles across time frames. These cost-efficient algorithms enable HitAlert to analyze incoming obstacles in real-time. Users could choose to receive an alert via sound, vibration, or HitAlert Band, a phone mounting peripheral belt that provides multi-channel, multi-level haptic feedback for precise notification. From our real scenario testing, HitAlert could detect incoming obstacles with a recall of 84%.

articleTitle: Extended Back-Off Range Doherty Power Amplifier with Flexible Phase Control
abstract: Due to the characteristic deviation of transistors under different working states, the output phases of the two sub-amplifiers under different biases and different input powers will be significantly different in back-off region, resulting in power loss and efficiency deterioration of Doherty power amplifiers (DPAs). In this regard, the power-dimension phase control mechanism is proposed. According to the output phase characteristics of sub-amplifiers in the extended back-off range of asymmetrical DPA, a tunable differential phase shifter is introduced to control the input phase differences in different states, so as to enhance the efficiency of Doherty power amplifiers. For verification, a DPA with flexible phase control is designed, fabricated and measured. The measured results show that the implemented DPA exhibits an extended back-off range of 9.5 dB over the frequency range from 3.2 GHz to 3.6 GHz, while the efficiency remains above 40% during the back-off region. With the proposed method, the DPA achieves an efficiency improvement up to 12% in wide back-off region.

articleTitle: Fuzzy and Ant Colony Optimization Based Clustering and Routing Protocol in Underwater Wireless Sensor Networks
abstract: This paper presents a Fuzzy C Means clustering algorithm for choosing the cluster head by first taking the cluster's center into account, and then relying on the nodes' remaining energy, for reliable and energy-efficient inter-cluster multi-hop routing from cluster heads to the surface sink node, Ant Colony Optimization is applied. A comparative analysis of the proposed protocol is done with the Single Hop Fuzzy Energy Efficient Routing protocol and Multi-Hop Fuzzy Energy Efficient Routing protocol. The proposed protocol outperforms SH-FEER and MH-FEER in FND up to 27.36%, in network lifetime up to 11.76%, and in energy consumption up to 25.91%.

articleTitle: Brain Hemorrhage Segmentation in CT Scan Images using Deep Learning based Approach
abstract: In this paper, a variety of neural networks are compared, and the optimal CE-Net model is found and improved. It can segment CT images of cerebral hemorrhage, especially for the small and irregular images.

articleTitle: Solving the Peak Load Problem of Online Charging System using Dynamic Reserve
abstract: In Online Charging System (OCS), to do charging and billing for many millions of customers, the availability of the system is important. At the peak load moment, a huge number of messages are sent to OCS simultaneously, causing performance degradation OCS. In this paper, we introduce a method using Dynamic Reserve to solve the peak load problems and improve the system's performance. The method uses a rule-based approach and combines both system status and business rules to bring really good performance. It improved the performance when reduced by 60% transactions per second (tps) and credit control request messages (CCR). Because of the rule-based approach, the method is reliable and is applied to real systems.

articleTitle: Gradual Drift Detection by Computing Outlier in Data Stream using Z-score
abstract: In data streaming scenario, data are created successively. And it is very common that the concepts of data may change at any positions in data stream. The properties of the target variables may shift between the static training data to real-world dynamic data. For changing the concepts, the learning performances are affected seriously. In addition, due to storage limitations, it is tough for an online learner to predict original labels of streaming data because of the concept drift as well as the location of drifting for data streaming. Therefore, a method that can detect the exact positions of drifts and quickly able to adapt changes for improving the learning performance is needed. As a solution, this paper presents a Gradual Drift Detection method for Data Stream using Z-score (DDZ) method. This DDZ approach uses Z-score to detect the stable positions of drifts in data stream. The proposed DDZ method adapts the changes very fast. As a result, DDZ is able to predict correct labels of instances and provide better outcomes. Four synthetic data stream generators with abrupt and gradual drifting and two real-world datasets are considered for evaluating the performance of the proposed method. The performance of the proposed DDZ method attains higher accuracy, recall and F-Score as compare to some existing drift detectors.

articleTitle: Ontology-based Methods for Healthcare System
abstract: Analytical in the healthcare arena involves data in a variety of formats, and organising them into understandable patterns is a difficult process. Data from numerous sources can be merged for interoperable access by using standard nomenclature. In this research, we use ontology approaches to model data by creating a domain ontology. The competency questions for domain ontology are designed to emphasise the significance of using ontology. A framework for evaluating domain experts is also discussed.

articleTitle: A Method for Selecting Relay Nodes in Delay Tolerant Network Routing U sing Periodicity
abstract: This paper aims to improve delivery probability and reduce the number of message drops by selecting relay nodes based on reachability. Currently, mobile terminals such as smartphones generally use a base station to transmit and receive data. However, communication becomes difficult when there is no coverage or when communication base stations do not function as usual due to natural disasters. Delay tolerant networks are expected to serve as alternative communications in times of disaster, etc. In delay tolerant network, routing is performed by stored delivery to cope with unstable connections. Stored delivery is a way of delivering data by storing it at a relay node while delivering it to another node. In this paper, we propose a routing method using a delay tolerant network focusing on periodic contacts. To evaluate the proposed method, we conducted an evaluation experiment using the simulator, giving the simulator about three weeks of contact data obtained in the real world. As a result, we confirmed that the proposed method improves the delivery probability compared to the previous method of delivering copies. The proposed method also showed a reduction in the number of messages dropped.

articleTitle: A Low Error Face Recognition System Based on A New Arrangement of Convolutional Neural Network and Data Augmentation
abstract: This paper represents a low error face recognition system constructed on convolutional neural network structure. The proposed method introduces a new layer arrangement for the CNN with added normalization layers. In addition, a data augmentation step consisting of vertical flip, scaling, rotation, and shift is implemented into the framework of our system to improve the accuracy. This augmentation helps the system to overcome the issue of having low number of samples per individuals in our dataset. The support vector machine (SVM) and Softmax are considered as classifiers of the proposed system, and results are evaluated for both classification methods. The system is tested on the ORL face image dataset. In our experiment SVM showed a higher accuracy compared to Softmax. The results compared to other existing face recognition methods show better performance and higher accuracy of the proposed system. The proposed method is evaluated with %50 of the dataset as training samples and the rest as test samples by random. Our technique achieves %98.64 with Softmax and %99.7 with SVM recognition rate.

articleTitle: Parameter Optimisation of LSTM Models in Stock Price Prediction
abstract: This study investigates the forecasting accuracies of Long Short-Term Memory models with different architectures and sheds light on the optimal combination of parameters when forecasting stock prices for the S&P500 fund.

articleTitle: Children's Behavior Analysis Through Smart Toys
abstract: Analyzing children's behavior is a major part of pediatric psychological studies. Here we are going to use the hand movements of the child to understand the behavioral pattern with the help of IoT-based toys.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Deep Semantic Segmentation Architectures for Disease Identification in Turmeric Crops
abstract: Semantic segmentation architectures are good in classification and localization of object boundaries in images. Four different architectures are chosen for segmentation and classification of diseased portion in turmeric crop. Quadrature Discriminant Feature Selection (QDFS) is implemented in one of the convolutional layers in all the architectures. This estimates an individual covariance matrix for every class and models non-linear relationships. The turmeric data set is huge and the feature set taken for classification is very large which increases the complexity of the networks. QDFS chooses the relevant features and eliminates the additional features. The results of classification are evaluated with metrics such as validation accuracy, Intersection over union, validation loss and dice coefficient. FCN8, PSP Net, Deep Lab V3 and MobileNetV3 (small) are the four architectures taken for comparative analysis. Real time dataset of about 4000 images is collected for the analysis. The observed results show that mobile Net v3 small has the highest validation accuracy and lowest validation loss with good intersection over union and Dice coefficient values.

articleTitle: Optimization of Dew Point, Humidity, and Temperature in Data Centers using Genetic Algorithm with Multiple Linear Regression
abstract: This study provides help in the Department of Public Works & Highways - Information Management Service Technology Support Division Systems Administration Section of the Philippines in bringing optimization analysis and metric standardization in their current data centers. The researchers proposes that the relationship between dew point, humidity and temperature be known in order to produce standards in maintaining the server reliability of their data centers. The researchers use a MATLAB program to create a genetic algorithm code in producing the best preferred optimization values with the help of the multiple linear regression as its fitness function. The results in the multiple linear regression analysis proved that there is a strong significant relationship between dew point (negative relationship) and humidity (positive relationship) to temperature based on its multiple r (correlation), r-squared and ANOVA- significance F. The generated optimized results from the MATLAB genetic algorithm code are the following; dew point be 12 degrees Celsius, humidity be in the range of 58 to 61 percent, and temperature be in the range of 20.027 to 20.253 degrees Celsius.

articleTitle: Optical Fiber based Nitrate Sensor using Mach-Zehnder Interferometer
abstract: An easily assembled and highly sensitive Mach-Zehnder interferometer (MZI) utilized fiber optic sensor coated with (polyvinyl alcohol) PVA and carbon nanotubes (CNTs)/PVA is proposed here for nitrate sensing. The sensor showed a sensitivity of 33.7 pm/ppm concerning nitrate solutions of 0 ppm to 50 ppm.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Comparative Analysis For Water Hyacinth Infestation With Automated Collector System
abstract: Water hyacinths have been abundant in Laguna Lake, covering about 9.4% of the area. It has environmental and harmful impacts on public health. The project uses machine learning technology to build a device that can monitor the infestation level and remove water hyacinths from the lake. It uses the Evolutionary Prototype Method to build a prototype that goes through a series of tests and refinements to complete. SVM (Support Vector Machine), KNN (K-Nearest Neighbor), and DT (Decision Tree) machine learning algorithms are compared to find the most effective algorithm to differentiate infestation levels of water hyacinth. Infestation levels are high, moderate, and low. Hyasense is a tool based on a traditional machine that collects water hyacinth manually. It equips a machine learning algorithm to harvest water hyacinth automatically. The most effective algorithm for classifying water hyacinth infestation is SVM, which has a range of 0.88–0.97 percent in its performance metrics (Precision, Recall, F1 Score, and Accuracy), almost twice the results of KNN and DT. Researchers can embed SVM on a device using Wi-Fi and Raspberry Pi. Hyasense is in working condition only if the infestation level is high and the storage area is not full. Remote monitoring of site infestation level, is achieved through a website that provides the most up-to-date collection status. Integrating machine learning technology into the system allows for automatic collection and remote monitoring of location. Adding sensors can improve the device.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Parameter Selection for Enhanced Edge Inference for a Multi-Output Regression model for Head Pose Estimation
abstract: Magnitude-based pruning is a technique used to optimise deep learning models for edge inference. We have achieved over 75% model size reduction with a higher accuracy than the original multi-output regression model for head-pose estimation.

articleTitle: Deep Learning of OpenStreetMap Images Labeled Using Road Traffic Accident Data
abstract: Identifying potentially high-risk areas is an important task for preventing road traffic accidents. In this paper, we present an attempt to train deep Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) on OpenStreetMap (OSM) images, each of which is labeled “high-risk” or “low-risk” using the data of road traffic accidents occurred in Okayama Prefecture, Japan from 2010 to 2021. It is shown that the trained CNNs can correctly predict whether a prescribed area is high-risk or low-risk only from the corresponding OSM image with a high probability. We also present some results of applications of Grad-CAM to the trained CNNs in order to visualize their decision making process.

articleTitle: Speed of Sound Self-compensated Video-rate Full-ring Ultrasound and Photoacoustic Computed Tomography
abstract: We developed a video-rate full-ring ultrasound and photoacoustic computed tomography (VF-USPACT) platform. The system is highlighted in in vivo imaging, including dual-contrasts, high spatial resolution, single-pulse photoacoustic imaging (< 50 µs), deep penetration (> 20mm), full view cross-sectional tomography (360°), and adaptive speed of sound compensation.

articleTitle: Design of a 980/1550-nm metasurface beam splitter and its application for EDFA
abstract: We propose two 980/1550-nm metasurface-based beam splitters for an EDFA system. As we know, this is the first scheme that applies metasurfaces in EDFA, and the simulation results show the transmission efficiency is over 50%.

articleTitle: Lightweight Networks for COVID-19 Detection from Chest X-Ray Images inside a Low-Tier Android Device
abstract: The efforts to inoculate majority of the population have been slower than expected and this is especially true for lower income countries. This problem has caused a lot of worries and further accentuates the importance of timely and effective mass testing considering the emergence of newer variants. The RT-PCR is still the gold standard diagnostic test for COVID-19 detection, but its limitations has led researchers and scientists to explore supplementary screening methods. One effective tool to consider is Chest X-Ray (CXR) imaging and combining it with deep learning has piqued attention from the artificial intelligence (AI) community. To further contribute to this research area, this work focuses on creating, evaluating, and comparing lightweight and mobile-phone-suitable COVID-detecting models. These transfer learning models together with their corresponding dynamic-range quantized versions are first tested according to their classification performance. Afterwards, the models are pushed in a low-tier phone to measure their resource consumption and inference timings. Results show that the utilization of EfficientNetB0 and MobileNetV3 (Small & Large) architectures for transfer learning without any quantization can produce at least 91 % overall average accuracy for 3-class classification scheme. For systems requiring more efficient models, using the quantized versions of the transfer learning models particularly with EfficientNetB0 and MobileNetV3Large as foundation can render at most 0.79 % accuracy loss but still show more than 95% f1-scores for the COVID-19 class.

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis of Machine Learning Algorithms for Bok Choy Leaf Disease Identification in Smart Aquaponics
abstract: Urban gardening innovation is driven by food scarcity. Smart aquaponics is one of the strategies utilized in urban farming. However, when plants and crops are infected, agricultural output is impacted. Farmers study plants visually for disease detection and identification. It is time-consuming, expensive, and inaccurate. A smart aquaponics system must be monitored, regulated, and automated to succeed. Using vision systems and machine learning algorithms to enhance farming is efficient. To do this, a comparison of three machine learning estimators was conducted: the Support Vector Machine (SVM), the Random Forest (RF), and the K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN). Each algorithm was modeled on Bok Choy leaves from a smart aquaponics system. Each model has been optimized to maximize hold-out validations. The results indicated that KNN with tuned hyperparameters was the most successful model for the dataset, with a mean accuracy of 98.21% for hold-out validation and 98.25% for classification.

articleTitle: Creducate: Blockchain-based Academic Record Management and Verification System Built in the Solana Network
abstract: Academic records are necessary requirements for employment and further studies. Despite being critical infor-mation that assesses one's eligibility in different disciplines, credentials are oftentimes difficult to acquire and inefficient to handle. Effectively, these manual and centralized processes make academic records vulnerable to fraudulent activities such as tampering and falsification. This project designed an academic record management and verification system using blockchain technology which offers enhanced security, immutability, trans-parency, and process improvement. Unlike previous works that used Bitcoin, Ethereum, or Hyperledger as their blockchain network, this project implemented its decentralized application (dApp) in the Solana network due to its faster processing speed, low-cost transaction fees, and expanding ecosystem. The dApp covers the generation, issuance, and verification of the most commonly requested credentials-the Transcript of Records (TORs) and diplomas. The intended users of this application are the universities, students, and third party entities that need to verify academic credentials for employment or other reasons. It was identified that the blockchain-based system provides a better means to (1) preserve the integrity of academic records, (2) transact between record handlers and requestors and (3) execute the processes of record generation and verification.

articleTitle: Quality Photo Sketch with Improved Deep Learning Structure
abstract: Drawing a sketched picture from realistic scene or photo is useful. In this paper, we propose a high-quality sketch generating model using deep convolutional neural network with self-attention structure. In style-transfer investigation, how to balance and retain both information details of input and style are what we want. For sketch drawing, edges or contours are the major components to form a sketch-like image. However, how to choose edges and contours are the major topics for the model to learn. Besides, keeping a small amount of texture and shadow can give a better view of a sketch result. We resolve this problem by proposing an end-to-end jump connection with elementwise multiplication instead of addition to keep texture details of the original input, which gives highlight of edges and contours for a sketch output. Experimental results show that our new design of network surpasses other state-of-the-art models in sketch details.

articleTitle: A Location Sensitive and Utility Based Advertising System for Public Transport
abstract: The increasing use of computers in vehicles presents opportunities to create value. Here we propose an advertising system that uses location and historical data for scheduling. Experiments indicate a good compromise between utility and fairness.

articleTitle: Detection of Geometry-based Adversarial Facial Attacks using Error Level Analysis
abstract: Despite Machine Learning (ML) and Deep Learning (DL) models in specific have achieved significant success in various applications of computer vision in recent years, they remain vulnerable to carefully crafted, human-invisible adversarial attacks. Adversarial attacks are generated intentionally by adding small perturbations to an input image to mislead the classifier. This paper investigates a new defense method against geometry-based adversarial face attacks that significantly mitigate the impact of such adversarial attacks on image-classification models. We generate geometry-based adversarial face images based on Fast Landmark Manipulation (FLM) method and Error Level Analysis (ELA) is performed to effectively discriminate adversarial face images from clean images. The performance of the proposed defense method is demonstrated on a real-world dataset with different types of classifiers. The experimental results show that our defense method can effectively detect adversarial face images from clean images with 99.75% accuracy.

articleTitle: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Solving Directed Steiner Tree Problems
abstract: The design of approximation algorithms for solving NP-hard Combinatorial Optimization (CO) problems is usually challenging. In recent years, deep learning has demonstrated the power to solve specific CO problems, such as Travelling Salesman problem and Minimum Vertex Cover problem. In this paper, we propose a deep reinforcement learning approach based on graph neural networks (GNN) to tackle Directed Steiner Tree (DST) problem. Simulations are conducted to evaluate the proposed approach compared to benchmarks upon approximation ratios and execution time respectively. The results reveal the potential of our approach in solving DST problems in practice and the scalability that can be smoothly applied to disparate graphs after enough off-line training.

articleTitle: Detecting and Locating Brain Tumors in Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) using an Adaptive Neuro Fuzzy Inference System (ANFIS)
abstract: Features extracted from contrast-limited adaptive histogram equalization (CLAHE) and Contrast-Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization (GLCM) and histogram-based features/non-GLCM are used as inputs for an Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference System (ANFIS)-based classifier for brain magnetic resonance images (MRI).

articleTitle: EraisNET: An Optical Flow based 3D ConvNET for Erasing Obstructions
abstract: Images captured from behind a fence, window, or during rain generally face occlusions. Though prior works have addressed the problems of individually de-raining, reflection, and occlusion removal, a common approach that removes all the obstruction has found little attention in the literature. In this paper, we address the image occlusion problem by proposing a deep learning-based approach wherein the proposed method uses motion differences between two images and extracts important moving features from videos to separate the background and the obstruction. To accomplish this task, a novel 3D-convolution architecture is introduced, which is trained with synthetically blended videos. We have used learned layer-based CNN methods combined with dense-optical flow with generative networks for better output images. Moreover, a dataset for obstruction removal with sequences for reflection and fencing removal is proposed. The proposed approach is well experimented over a different variety of images and is found as a good candidate against state-of-the-art schemes.

articleTitle: Traffic Priority based Forwarder Selection for Data Routing in Mobile WBANs
abstract: The popularity of the wireless body area network (WBAN) enables us to think about the future new normal form in the healthcare domain. WBAN, with miniature sensors placed in the human body, measures the physiological sign of the patient body and sends the data to the hospitals and health units via access points. WBAN can easily be adopted for body-to-body communication due to freely changing its position, associating or disassociating with its neighbors. In this situation, low delay and reliable data transmission have brought challenges to WBAN data routing. In the past year, various routing protocols have been proposed to address these challenges. In this work, a tuning-based forwarder selection algorithm is proposed with the aim to minimize delay and routing overhead in data transmission. In our work, the coordinator in a WBAN chooses its forwarder based on the priority of the packet in its transmission queue. An efficient cost function is designed by taking into account both delay and stability metrics. In the proposed work, the coordinator with high priority traffic selects a low delay forwarder, while the coordinator with low priority traffic chooses a stable next hop node as the forwarder. We assess the performance of the proposed tuning-based forwarder selection via extensive simulations and compare it with the existing forwarder selection algorithms. As per the result, we achieved better performance by our proposed method than the existing algorithms.

articleTitle: Multilateration-based Machine Learning for Indoor Localization
abstract: Indoor Positioning Systems (IPS) are becoming increasingly beneficial as they can provide real-time location data to improve various workflows. Their accuracies can be improved by deploying machine learning solutions to serve as the positioning engine. Fingerprinting-based models have been widely proposed as they can utilize the available network devices as reference nodes to build a wireless signal profile of the location. However, this approach requires repetitive manual data collection, which may not be feasible in restricted spaces and is impractical for off-the-shelf consumer solutions. This paper therefore proposes an alternative multilateration-based machine learning model trained on a minimal training set. Experimental results showed that the proposed trilateration-based model outperformed both the traditional multilateration and the fingerprinting-based models.

articleTitle: A Data-Centric and Dynamic-Range based Misbehavior Detection Approach for VANET
abstract: Evolution in vehicular applications enhances the need for correct and accurate information transmission among the vehicles in the Vehicular Ad-hoc Network (VANET). The vehicle mobility data, road conditions and critical environmental information are communicated over the network using V2X (Vehicle to Everything) communication. Some inside VANET nodes transmit implausible data by using their network access credentials. They misbehave by making fake alerts regarding accidents and traffic congestion. Such misbehavior should be detected using data-centric or node-centric misbehavior detection approaches. We propose a data-centric detection mechanism employing some consistency and plausibility checks. Additionally, we create a real-time attack-wise labelled dataset for ten different types of attacks in a real road scenario in Jaipur city. We simulate the proposed mechanism on the generated real-time dataset and then conduct a comparative study of the mechanism performance in an Indian and a foreign road scenario. In both cases, the proposed system is capable of detecting significant attacks, but the results vary because of the differences in the two scenarios.

articleTitle: Program for the Task Allocation Model: Integrating Workforce Planning for Manpower Utilization at City of Cabuyao Engineering Office
abstract: The City Engineering Office has such a great deal of difficulty completing projects, and when new ones come up, the work piles up. The results of a survey of 7 individuals who work for the program for projects on the causes of pending allocation delays indicate that labor capacity of the engineering office is one of the most significant factors in increasing pending allocation. The right quality and number of people are required for firms to successfully implement strategic planning. It requires the correct quantity of workforce with the right skills and talents at the appropriate times, in proper position, and for the cheapest price, among other things. Through an Integrated Workforce Planning Model, the proponents are led to the intervention of an allocation system through the use of Excel Visual Basic Application. The data collected was used and analyzed in order to build the system by considering the workforce analysis, computation of utilization points based on the set parameters of budget and estimated duration and the current classified description of the construction projects at the City Engineering Office. It was found out that workforce planning was an effective tool for optimizing the capacity of people working on programs to meet the demands of construction projects.

articleTitle: Development of Standard Operator Instruction Sheet (OIS) to Improve Productivity in Seiren Production Department at Ohtsuka Poly-Tech Philippines Inc
abstract: The Ohtsuka Poly-Tech Philippines, Inc. Seiren Department processes cutting as one of the three processes involving a range of machinery, including specialized cutting, and forming machinery. The objective of this study is to develop a standard Operator-Instruction-Sheet (OIS) to increase production productivity. A time study were done to determine the timing requirements for each phase as the researchers followed the steps of the flowcharts using the Eliminate-Combine-Rearrange-and-Simplify (ECRS) method. Based on the result, productivity of the preformer process, special process productivity, and ribbon process productivity increased by 12.79<sup>%</sup>, 4<sup>%</sup>, and 0.4<sup>%</sup> respectively.

articleTitle: Anomaly Detection in Red Reflex Images Using Deep Learning Approaches
abstract: Amblyopia is a noteworthy disease in children leading to visual loss. This work focuses on creating a deep learning model for the detection of Amblyopia factors in patients wearing masks under the COVID-19 pandemic.

articleTitle: Integrated Visual-Based ASL Captioning in Videoconferencing Using CNN
abstract: An assistive videoconferencing tool that combines hand tracking, region extraction, and a convolutional neural network (CNN) for gesture recognition has been developed to improve accessibility for sign language users.

articleTitle: A Conceptual Architecture for AI in Supply Chain Risk Management
abstract: A high-level conceptual architecture is proposed for Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Supply Chain Risk Management (SCRM) based on literature review and qualitative research. It incorporates architecture components across data management, model development, and model deployment.

articleTitle: Adoption of big data by global chemical industries
abstract: The new era of big data is influencing the chemical industry tremendously, providing several opportunities to reshape its operations. However, given the development of big data, the availability of free software, and the large amount of real- time data generated and stored, the chemical industry is still not fully adopting big data. Moreover, the industry is just starting to realise the importance of the large amount of data it owns to assist in making the right decisions and support its strategies. Therefore, this article explores the significance and influence of identified gap variables, namely professional competencies, business intelligence, data scalability, process monitoring, and investment in tools, for the adoption of big data in the chemical industry. This study follows a survey-based quantitative method using structural equation modelling. The data collected was studied to draw scientific conclusions about the myriad of hypothesised relationships. This was accomplished by employing a positivist paradigm in the research process. This study recognises the strong relationship between data scalability, process monitoring, and the investment in tools for big data adoption as a contribution towards industry application and practice. Mediation effects between the constructs and final measures were studied as part of this research, and the significance of their relationships was established. This study contributes to the application of the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology. Based on the literature survey and research outcomes, this study also positions the chemical industry in Davenport and Harris's paradigm of analytical maturity. This article's conclusions and contributions towards practical application are expected to support a shift from conventional methods towards a data-driven approach to decision-making in the chemical industry. To further achieve the objectives, conclusions, and future research directions presented in this article, suggest government, academia, and industry must work together to overcome all present and potential challenges.

articleTitle: Theory-Guided Bayesian Analysis for Modeling Impact of COVID-19 on Gross Domestic Product
abstract: GDP or Gross Domestic Product is a key indicator of economic status, which provides an omni-comprehensive measure of the wealth of a country or a state. With the sudden proliferation of novel coronavirus disease (COVID-19), there has been increasing interest in forecasting GDP, since this may be severely impacted by the various pandemic control measures imposed in recent days. An accurate forecast of GDP can extensively help in putting forth right administrative measures while ensuring minimum disruption in economy. Though the recent researches focus on various machine learning-based data-driven models for this purpose, these primarily analyze the change in observed GDP data without explicitly modeling the pandemic impact. We address this issue by proposing a novel approach that incorporates epidemiological insights into Bayesian network-based predictive analytics to account for the influence of COVID-19 development on the GDP. Rigorous experimentation on state-level and country-level datasets of India demonstrates that a judicious combination of theoretical and data-driven models can substantially improve GDP forecast performance. Our model produces an average prediction error of 0.002% and outperforms several state-of-the-art techniques with a large margin.

articleTitle: Real-Time GICP: Direct LiDAR SLAM for CPU Environment
abstract: As a core part in modern Robotics research, Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) is widely used in different kinds of autonomous robots, such as autonomous vehicles. Existing direct methods and feature-based methods in LiDAR-SLAM still have different limitations. In this paper, we propose a lightweight, robust and accurate LiDAR-SLAM framework named Real-Time GICP, which contains improved GICP method as front-end and Scan-Context loop detection to construct pose graph optimization. Experimental results show that Real-Time GICP can achieve state-of-the-art accuracy and superior computational efficiency comparing with other open-source GICP methods. Our method can achieve around 50 Hz for 64 rings Velodyne LiDAR with Intel i7 CPU, which makes Real-Time GICP more efficient in when deployed on popular robotics computational platforms.

articleTitle: Lettuce Root Development and Monitoring System Using Machine Learning in Hydroponics
abstract: Roots of a hydroponically grown lettuce are usually susceptible to waterborne diseases like Pythium disease (root rot). Visual inspection of a plant root is needed in a hydroponic system to determine the health status of the plant. However, removing the plants in its growing environment will stress the plants that can cause stunted growth, and is susceptible to further complications once the roots are exposed outside the environment. Also, studying the development of the lettuce roots on its freshness could help to set standards in determining its shelf life and could lead to a longer life. The project intends to develop an automated root monitoring system for detecting root rot and changing water temperature to avoid extreme heat that damages the root system, affecting the entire plant. The Peltier module was employed to keep the water temperature stable between 18°C – 26°C. If the water temperature exceeds this range, the system will react based on what is best for the plant. The researchers used a camera to monitor the roots across the three grow boxes for the root detecting method. The researchers also implemented image pre-processing, specifically cropping and resizing, to improve image quality in preparation for image processing, and the Decision Tree method for machine learning. The model detected root rot with 91 % accuracy. The system was able to accurately identify and locate roots as well as predict their health status.

articleTitle: Front Matter

articleTitle: A Reconfigurable Submillimeter-Wave Polarizer Based on Phase-Change Materials
abstract: A reconfigurable sub millimeter-wave polarizer based on phase-change materials is presented in the work. The polarizer consists of7×7 microstrip patch units. The patch in the unit is excited by the slot on the bottom layer. Four corners of the patch are coated with GeTe phase-change materials. By changing the state of the GeTe through laser, the polarizer can convert the linear polarization to left-hand and right-hand circular polarization. The polarizer has an impedance bandwidth of 6.4<sup>%</sup> from 96 to 102.4 GHz and an axial-ratio bandwidth of 8.4% from 96 to 104.4 GHz. The proposed polarizer has potential applications in imaging, tomography, sensing, and 6G communication.

articleTitle: Self-Organizing Multi-hop LoRa Mesh Network for Wide Area Air Quality Monitoring
abstract: Current LoRa technology does not fully support mesh networks. We adapted AODV mechanisms to develop a self-healing, multi-hop LoRa-based network protocol. We validated its performance on an air quality monitoring sensor network.

articleTitle: Electrically Small Huygens Dipole Antenna Based Rectenna and Array for Wireless Power Transfer Enabled Internet-of-Things Applications
abstract: This paper introduces the electrically small Huygens dipole antenna (HDA) based rectenna and antenna array for wireless power transfer (WPT) enabled Internet-of-Things (IoT) applications. WPT -enabled IoT applications require two major sub-systems as the receiving rectenna and the wireless energy transmitting antenna array. The developed electrically small Huygens dipole antenna (HDA) is the ideal candidate for enabling both sub-systems thanks to its ultracompact size and unidirectional Huygens radiation pattern with wide half-power beamwidth. An ultracompact and highly efficient wireless power capturing rectenna was designed by seamlessly integrating a compact rectifier circuit to the HDA. Moreover, to realize long distance WPT and cover large area simultaneously, a linear-array with beam-steering performance was developed and also based on the HDA element. They are ideal candidate for WPT-enabled battery-free IoT ecosystems.

articleTitle: 3D Object Tracking with Reduced Cumulative Error on Sparse Point Clouds
abstract: In 3D target tracking, the cumulative error generated in the sparse point cloud environment makes tracking more difficult, which is a key issue to track the target stably to allow the lost target to be retrieved. This paper proposes a Bayesian theorem-based 3D single-target tracking algorithm to improve the subsequent tracking performance by reducing the cumulative error caused by low-quality prior information. First, we use Bayes' theorem to classify the prior information to obtain the maximum a posteriori probability, and second, we suppress the proposals with poor prior information to re-duce the cumulative error. Finally, the algorithm proposed in this paper is applied to the dataset, and the study shows an improvement of about 23% in real-time performance over the PTT-Net algorithm and excellent performance in several tracking metrics.

articleTitle: Electro-optic characterization of thin-film lithium niobate modulators at frequencies up to 325 GHz
abstract: We charaterize the mmWave-optic modulation performances of thin-film lithium niobate modulators at frequencies up to 325 GHz with a measured 3-dB electro-optic bandwidth of 170 GHz and a 6-dB bandwidth of 295 GHz. The device also shows a low RF half-wave voltage of 8.3 V measured at an ultrahigh modulation frequency of 250 GHz.

articleTitle: Hysteresis-free behavior of MoS2 negative capacitance transistor by using low-temperature grown HfO2 as encapsulation layer
abstract: A MoS<inf>2</inf> negative-capacitance field-effect transistor (NCFET) with 6-nm Hf<inf>0.5</inf>Zr<inf>0.5</inf>O<inf>2</inf>(HZO) as ferroelectric layer and 2-nm Al<inf>2</inf>O<inf>3</inf> as dielectric layer plus a 2-nm low-temperature grown HfO<inf>2</inf> as encapsulation layer is fabricated. Improved device performance, especially hysteresis behavior, is obtained as compared to its counterpart without the encapsulation layer: an almost hysteresis-free behavior (5–20 mV), a subthreshold swing of 36.2 mV/dec and an on/off current ratio of <tex>$2.8\times 10^{7}$</tex>. The improved hysteresis should be associated with enhanced screen effects on charged-impurity scattering and protection from absorption of environmental gas/water molecules by the thin high <tex>$k$</tex> encapsulation.

articleTitle: Few-shot learning for Defect Detection of Industrial Components
abstract: Benefiting from a large amount of labeled data, deep learning has attracted widespread attention for its excellent performance. This great success is inseparable from the support of the supervision of massive data. However, in industrial defect detection scenarios, the cost of collecting and labeling large amounts of data is quite high. Therefore, this paper explores a limited-data regime to build a more efficient defect detection model. To this end, we propose a defect-based location augmentation method to increase the diversity of training data and improve the performance of defect detection models. The scheme based on defect location augmentation greatly increases the diversity of training data, which alleviates the overfitting problem of insufficient training data. Experimental results show that the proposed method can well recognize the defect types of industrial components when only one shot defect data is available.

articleTitle: Universal Energy Access: Enhancing Networked Rural Electrification Using Modified Fuzzy Inference Method
abstract: To achieve UN Sustainable Development Goal 7 (SDG7) by 2030, better rural electrification is required. Most current projects provide electricity inefficiently to rural users rather using stand-alone designs. As most remaining unserved users are located in difficult-to-reach areas, IEA has pointed out that the marginal cost of rural electrification is increasing. Earlier work indicates that networking rural villages would be more cost-effective than prior models. This work uses modified fuzzy inference to improve power distribution costs by improving the optimality of distribution network design.

articleTitle: Soliton microcombs in silicon-carbide microresonators
abstract: We demonstrate SiC-based soliton microcombs operated at room temperature - a key step for integrated SiC nonlinear photonics for frequency metrology applications. We have successfully routed and switched among different soliton states using an auxiliary laser to optically counteract the thermo-optic effect. In addition to single soliton generation, we further observe a wideband comb spectra translation from near-infrared to visible via the second-order nonlinearity, key for the realization of on-chip f -to-2f self-referencing,

articleTitle: Novel Strategies for DAC based Offset Elimination Technique in Resistive Bridge Sensor
abstract: Resistive sensors are beneficial for monitoring physical parameters such as temperature, pressure, humidity, or different pressure wave-based biological signals. Traditionally, resistive sensors generate significant low-frequency offset voltage due to their resistance variation with external factors. Offset is responsible for performance degradation and increased power dissipation of the whole system. This brief analyzed the ‘developed offset’ in constant voltage and constant current-based excitation. The programmable current generation technique based on a digital to analog converter (DAC) can eliminate the generated offset effectively. Different variations of DAC, related supporting structures are developed in 0.18µm, 1.8 V process and analyzed for their compensation capability based on parameters like area, power consumption, and ease of implementation. The area of the overall system and no. of bits in DAC are improved by 15% and 2-bit, respectively for the proposed architecture w.r.t state-of-the-art design for an equal amount of offset compensation. However, the complexity of the compensating architecture is increased due to an increase in the supporting architecture of DAC.

articleTitle: Model-free computer-generated holography
abstract: We propose using reinforce algorithm as a model-free method to synthesize computer-generated holograms. We show in simulation that our method reconstructs holograms with comparable fidelity as prevalent model-based method.

articleTitle: Reed-Muller Sequence-Based Unsourced Random Access over Multipath Fading Channels
abstract: An unsourced random access scheme using the second-order Reed-Muller (RM) sequences is proposed. Each of the active devices maps its message to an RM sequence and randomly selects a single subcarrier to transmit through a multipath fading channel. In a receiver, after OFDM demodulation, at each subcarrier the list of corresponding messages is blindly decoded by iterative RM decoding. Simulations show that the proposed systems provide low block error rates over multipath fading channels.

articleTitle: Facial Expression Recognition Based on Data Augmentation and Swin-Transformer
abstract: We propose a Transformer-based facial expression detection framework, combining different data enhancement methods with pre-trained model, achieves the best performance compared with other baselines.

articleTitle: Characterization, Analysis and Optimization of a CMOS RF Energy Harvesting Rectifier System for WSN Application
abstract: Wireless Power Transfer has become an important aspect in energy harvesting to supply ultra-low power sensor networks. In remote areas, energy sources become a significant restriction for sensors. This paper presents an analysis and optimization technique for RF Energy harvesting system for Wireless Local Area Network (WLAN) source operating at 2.4GHz to power sensor node applications. The rectifier which is the main component for energy conversion features a multi-stage cross-coupled differential-drive architecture with single-sided biasing and storage capacitors on each stage to help improve the rectifier performance by adding instantaneous RF voltage at each stage. The architecture is implemented in standard 65nm CMOS Technology. The measurements were done by using input RF signal frequency of 2.4GHz for resistive load values of 30k, 100k and 1M Ohm. The proposed design system verification is used to analyze and investigate the effect and importance of layout and package parasitic impedances to the rectifier output voltage, sensitivity, and power conversion efficiency (PCE). Measurement results of <tex>$\boldsymbol{\text{Rload}=100\mathrm{k}\Omega}$</tex> and <tex>$\boldsymbol{\mathbf{Cload}=10\text{pF}}$</tex> showed an output voltage of 1 V at −10dBm input power and 23.93% PCE.

articleTitle: Recent Advances in Three-Dimensional Frequency Selective Structures
abstract: Frequency-selective structure (FSS) is a periodic artificial structure that can produce electromagnetic selectivity. Conventionally, it consists of single- or multi-layer elements periodically arranged in a plane, which can manipulate spatial electromagnetic waves under different frequencies, polarizations, and angles of incidence. Various types of structures, analysis theories, and design methods have been developed for conventional FSSs. Unfortunately, these conventional surfaces manipulate electromagnetic waves through their 2-D or 2.5-D periodic elements, thus leading to serious limitations to their filtering performance and design flexibilities. Recently, a new class of 3-D FSS, consisting of 3-D multimode elements of waveguide cavities or transmission-line structures, has attracted much attention. Owing to this special construction of periodic elements, 3-D FSSs can provide more degrees of freedom in the spatial dimensions to exhibit superior performance features. This paper aims to provide a review of recent 3-D FSSs based on slot-lines with a focus on the state-of-the-art techniques in the design and exploration of bandpass FSSs and wideband polarizers.

articleTitle: Design of a Power Efficient Accelerator for Reconstructing Videos from Gaussian Mixture Model Data
abstract: The Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM) is a compressive sensing (CS) technique which can effectively reduce the sizes of video files. However, reconstructing a GMM-based CS video is very time-consuming because it usually involves a process with high computational complexity. In this paper, we re-design the reconstruction flow to make it hardware friendly and implement a power-efficient accelerator based on this modified flow. The proposed accelerator, with the power consumption of only 1.5 Watts, can complete reconstruction tasks 25.07 times faster than a server-class CPU for a CS stream with a resolution of 300×400 pixels.

articleTitle: Balancing Privacy Preservation and Utility in Anti-Face Detection Systems
abstract: The advancement in facial detection has led to increased privacy concerns as it can potentially lead to ma-licious activities such as identity theft and illegal surveillance. Hence, several anti-face detection systems have been developed to address this concern. However, existing systems are trained end-to-end and do not give information as to how image features e.g. resolution, texture, and color can contribute to detection/misdetection. In this work, we find the significant image features in predicting the minimum Gaussian noise, <tex>$sigma_{min}$</tex>, necessary to avoid face detection. Three regression models were trained to determine the minimum level of perturbation. The multilayer perceptron (MLP) regression model exhibited the best performance, with 38.02 % of the detected faces being effectively concealed. The results from this study show that the image features such as local binary pattern, width, value, and height significantly impacted the predicted values of sigma, and can be used to accurately determine the minimum level of Gaussian noise to prevent face detection systems from detecting faces in images.

articleTitle: Leaky Mode Radiation Properties of Dielectric Loaded Helix
abstract: In this paper, a full wave analytical theory has been established in order to determine the radiation properties of the dielectric loaded helix (DLH) in leaky mode configurations. The dispersion diagram, which establishes the axial phase propagation constant as a function of frequency, is used to categorize the guided and leaky mode region. By taking into account, electric and magnetic field vector potentials as well as the polarization current approach, the analytical theory of radiation is developed. According to the guided mode's and leaky mode's respective modal dispersion properties, the radiation pattern in end-fire direction and broadside direction is calculated and described. The calculated axial phase constants have been used to identify the electric and magnetic field components at a given frequency, which have then been translated into electric and magnetic field potentials and, ultimately, radiation characteristics. This type of geometry is useful for designing wideband leaky wave antennas.

articleTitle: Utilization of Food Waste and Wood Ash in Manufacturing 2-in-1 Fertilizer Through Aerobic Composting
abstract: One of our country's most pressing challenges has always been proper waste disposal. It is one of the most common human-caused environmental issue that is undoubtedly hard to manage. Most of the garbage like food waste always end up on roadsides, landfills and others; and as the human population increase, the pollution also increases. Based from City Environment and Natural Resources Office (CENRO), Brgy. Mamatid generates a total of 15,591.43kg of biodegradable waste daily which is the highest contributor in Cabuyao City. These biodegradable components include food waste, such as high-nutrient fruits and vegetables, which may be found in the barangay's public marketplace, where many people allege that there is no waste management system. The goal of this research is to recycle Brgy. Mamatid's food waste which will be converted into a useful 2-in-1 organic fertilizer through aerobic composting and mixing with wood ash. To determine the optimal N-P-K amount for fertilizer, the researchers used a number of experimental methods which is factor to be considered in manufacturing fertilizer. In addition, the researchers undertake DIY testing to determine the effectiveness of wood ash in pest control.

articleTitle: Hindi Spoken Conversational System for Healthcare Humanoid
abstract: As the world is advancing in robotics, humanising the robot is one of the focused areas. In this work, we show-case our Hindi Spoken Conversational System deployed Mitra robot. The Hindi Spoken Conversational system includes speech recoznition, conversational AI and speech synthesis systems.

articleTitle: Ground Fissure Detection System using Raspberry Pi and Drone Technology
abstract: Ground fissure results in a significant risk to animals, humans, and infrastructure. The conventional method for indirect georeferencing of remote sensing images cannot meet the timeliness requirements due to its processing speed. This study focuses on a Ground Fissure Detection System to efficiently provide data about existing ground fissures for thorough research of the experts. It also aims to provide a 2D mapping of the area and have approximation length and width of the fissures that will be useful for risk and evacuation planning. The detection accuracy and speed of the system are based on the evaluation and training of models, and testing in an actual site in Lemery, Batangas. The SSD MobileNet algorithm was used for fissure detection with detection accuracy of 59.37% at 39ms processing speed.

articleTitle: Integrating Low-Cost LiDAR and Stereo Camera for 3D Object Detection with Lidar-Stereo Fusion and Cost Volume Enhancement
abstract: We propose a fusion network that integrates LiDAR and stereo images multiple times for 3D object detection. It fuses projected left/right LiDAR maps with stereo camera images at the beginning of the network, then adopts the LiDAR maps again for cost volume enhancement with a novel parallel fusion network (PFNet). The PFNet combines two distinctive strategies: a learnable strategy and a physical modeling strategy. The learnable design modifies HeirCCVNorm (Hierarchical Conditional Cost Volume Normalization). The physical modeling involves Gaussian embedding of LiDAR signals. Our simulations showed that the proposed network has better 3D object detection performance than a recent acclaimed state-of-the-art method when using the same dataset for training.

articleTitle: Wafer-scale thin-film lithium niobate device fabrication and characterization
abstract: Lithium niobate is an excellent optical material and is of great significance for future photonic integrated circuits. This work studies the wafer-scale fabrication of thin-film lithium niobate devices and demonstrates a robust process flow to realize photonic elements with optical loss of − 0.1 dB/cm.

articleTitle: 3D-printed High-Gain Wideband Antenna Arrays for Millimeter-Wave Applications
abstract: The millimeter-wave high-gain wideband antenna arrays with dual- and linearly-polarized radiation realized by the three-dimensional (3D) printing technology are summarized in this paper. The dual-polarized magneto-electric (ME) dipole and horn antennas serving as the radiating elements are fed by the air-filled full-corporate feed networks. A novel air-filled differential feeding cavity loaded with a shorted-ended cross-shaped waveguide are employed to widen the bandwidth for the array with dual-polarization. In view of the theoretical analysis based on the one-time-reflection circuit model, the X-junctions and multi-reflection-nulls T -junctions are respectively cascaded to form the X-type and H-type topology full-corporate feed networks in order to achieve bandwidth enhancement for the large-scale array. The measured results of the three arrays have confirmed that the 3D-printed arrays are attractive candidate for various millimeter-wave wireless applications.

articleTitle: Performance Comparison of Machine Learning Algorithms in Dementia Classification Using Electroencephalogram Decomposition
abstract: Dementia has significant social and economic impacts on direct medical, social, and informal care costs. An effective diagnostic method may provide an early diagnosis of the disease, giving a leeway to tackle the burden. This paper presents a performance comparison of five machine learning techniques for dementia classification based on a feature extraction method using cardinal-spline empirical mode decomposition (CS-EMD) of electroencephalogram (EEG). The comparison was validated using repeated k-fold cross-validation and the Wilcoxon signed-rank test. The top two classifiers are artificial neural network (ANN) and support vector machine (SVM), with no statistically significant difference in performance in terms of overall accuracy. The ANN and SVM achieved average classification accuracies of 93% and 88.42%, respectively, outperforming discriminant analysis, the K-nearest neighbors, and the naïve Bayes classifier in the repeated k-fold CV. Furthermore, the ANN classifier in a train/test split test produced higher accuracy and sensitivity rates, but lower specificity and precision than the SVM. The results show good potential for the CS-EMD-based features of EEG decomposition and machine learning classifiers, such as ANN and SVM, in dementia diagnostic applications.

articleTitle: A Trainable Sequence Learner that Learns and Recognizes Two-Input Sequence Patterns
abstract: We present two designs for an analog circuit that can learn to detect a temporal sequence of two inputs. The training phase is done by feeding the circuit with the desired sequence and, after the training is completed, each time the trained sequence is encountered again the circuit will emit a signal of correct recognition. Sequences are in the order of tens of nanoseconds. The first design can reset the trained sequence on runtime but assumes very strict timing of the inputs. The second design can only be trained once but is lenient in the input's timing.

articleTitle: Threat detection in Cognitive radio networks using SHA-3 algorithm
abstract: Cognitive Radio Network makes intelligent use of the spectrum resources. However, spectrum sensing is vulnerable to numerous harmful assaults. To lower the network's performance, hackers attempt to alter the sensed result. In the fusion centre, blockchain technology is used to make broad judgments on spectrum sensing in order to detect and thwart hostile activities. The sensed local results are hashed using the SHA 3 technique. This improves spectrum sensing precision and effectively thwarts harmful attacks. In comparison to other established techniques like equal gain combining, the simulation results demonstrate higher detection probability and sensing precision. Thus, employing Blockchain technology, cognitive radio network security can be significantly enhanced.

articleTitle: Vision-based Hand Gesture Interface for Real-time Computer Operation Control
abstract: Humans typically perform simple actions with hand gestures. If a computer interprets gestures, then human-computer interaction can be enhanced. This paper proposes hand gesture-based interface for controlling computer operations using deep learning and custom dataset.

articleTitle: Combining Photonic Blind Source Separation and Genetic Algorithm for Mode-Division-Multiplexed Fiber Communications
abstract: We demonstrate the combination of photonic blind source separation with genetic algorithm to unscramble modal crosstalk in mode-division-multiplexed fiber transmissions. We achieve a high signal quality with MSE of 0.03% and fast convergence time of 10 µs.

articleTitle: A Data Traffic Remapping Scheme for Delay Sensitive Industrial Applications
abstract: Network topology configuration in an Edge Infrastructure-as-a-Service (EIaaS) paradigm consists of Edge Computational Nodes (ECNs) placement at optimal locations and balanced assignment of IoT nodes among ECNs. The existing ECN placement and mapping schemes perform the IoT-ECN mapping based on the historic/fixed/single-instance data traffic of IoT nodes. These schemes suffer from issues such as increased delay, unbalanced data traffic distribution etc., when data traffic pattern deviates from the initial settings. This work proposes an extension of our previous work, named as Extended-Cost Aware Edge Computational Node Placement (EcoECNP) scheme, to address the mentioned issues under varying (query-based) data traffic scenarios. The scheme utilizes the common nodes (received from the mapping module of coECNP) and their traffic (obtained from requested data traffic) for remapping among ECNs to achieve balanced data traffic distribution among ECNs and minimize the delay. The performance evaluation indicates that the proposed scheme reduces the average delay per IoT node by 10%-53% and achieves 25%-68% more balanced data traffic distribution among ECNs than state-of-the-art schemes under varying data traffic scenarios.

articleTitle: Effects of Iron (III) Oxide-Enhanced Building Materials on RF Communications
abstract: Electromagnetic performance of iron (III) oxide-enhanced building material prototypes are accessed at mid-band 5G frequencies using free-space method. <tex>$\mathbf{S}_{21}$</tex> data show that up to 2.2 dB improvement was achieved with optimal volumetric fraction of 2-wt%.

articleTitle: A General Method of Time Delay Estimation and Compensation Based on CNN in Optical Parallel Channels
abstract: A general time delay estimation and compensation method based on multi-path effect analyses and convolutional neural network (CNN) for synchronization of optical parallel channels is proposed. Experimental verification is conducted in a 16-channel 400G system, and the root mean squared error (RMSE) of predicted time delay is 4.81ps, which meets the requirement for no error bit.

articleTitle: Measurement of Wrist Pulse Using Fiber Optic MZI for Analysis of Heart Rate and Respiration Rate
abstract: Fiber-optic Mach-Zehnder interferometer (MZI)-based wrist pulse sensors can be used to monitor heart rate (HR) and respiration rate (RR) simultaneously. The HR and RR calculations of the sensor have very little error with the reference signals.

articleTitle: Multi-Wavelength Silicon Photonic Neural Network for WDM Optical Communication Systems
abstract: We propose and demonstrate a photonic recurrent neural network which can simultaneously compensate for fiber dispersion and nonlinearity in WDM communication systems in the photonic domain. The resulted Q-factor outperforms some conventional DSP methods.

articleTitle: Restroom Hygiene Smart Monitoring System Incorporating Lora Technology
abstract: This paper proposed LoRa based system using Wide area networking (WAN) protocol built on top of the LoRa radio modulation operated by a cloud server with a low power battery and operating at long distance.

articleTitle: F-GAN: Real-Time Color Correction Model of Underwater Images
abstract: In recent years, color correction of underwater images is becoming a hot research field due to the wide application of Autonomous Underwater Vehicles and Remotely Operated Vehicles in monitoring marine environments. Many kinds of deep learning models have been presented by researchers to correct the color of the underwater images to facilitate the work of both people and machines. However, these models emphasize the correction effect more, and they can't be applied to real-time scenarios, especially for high-resolution images (480*640). Therefore, we propose a more concise generative adversarial network-based model to achieve real-time color correction of underwater images. To supervise the training process better, we design a multiterm loss function including adversarial loss, content loss, and structural similarity loss to estimate the generated image quality. Experiments on the EUVP (Enhancing Underwater Visual Perception) dataset show that our approach produces visually satisfactory results for high-resolution images under the real-time requirement. Besides, our method can even outperform some state-of-the-art models.

articleTitle: e-Barter: A Mobile-based Trading Platform
abstract: Bartering is more than a century-old form of exchanging goods or services among traders that does not involve money as a form of payment. This is no longer a common practice in commerce nowadays but that does not mean that this form of trading is obsolete. Some are still engaged into this form of trading and uses social media as platform for informal barter trade. Given this disconnect between current technology and the barter system has led to the creation of e-Barter, a mobile application that host online auction and trading as its main objective. Prototyping methodology was used during the development and in the process so specific objectives were met such as identifying the features of an electronic barter system and the appropriate platform for the development was identified. E-Barter was validated through user acceptance testing gaining a grand mean of 4.62 interpreted as Highly Acceptable in terms of functionality, usability, reliability, portability, and over-all acceptance of the 20 respondents coming from IT field and prospective users. Considering that the main reason why barter occurred long time ago is due to lack of money, e-Barter can be a support for them to address their needs or resolve the idea of utilizing the things they no longer need and exchange it for something useful without involving money in the transaction. Thus, help them save money for the things that they need to acquire.

articleTitle: Perfect vortex beam generators enabled by fiber-tip metasurface
abstract: We demonstrate two perfect vortex beam generators based on the fiber-tip metasurface. The ring radius of the generated beam is verified to be independent of the topological charge through numerical simulations.

articleTitle: 1.7-µm all-fiber laser system for stimulated Raman scattering microscopy
abstract: We present an 80-MHz 1.7-µm all-fiber laser system. With a peak power of 1318 kW, the laser system can realize stimulated Raman scattering microscopy in cell-silent regime according to our prior work.

articleTitle: Broadband antireflection metasurface based on quasi-random dielectric Mie resonators
abstract: Minimizing undesired reflection is important for solar cell applications. Recently, high-index dielectric Mie resonator has attracted significant attention due to its efficient light trapping and antireflection performance. However, for such Mie-resonant ultrathin antireflection coating, properties presenting both a uniform low-valued reflectance curve and a large bandwidth are difficult to be satisfied simultaneously. Here, we demonstrate a strategy to achieve broadband antireflection using quasi-random Mie resonators. Different shapes of Mie resonators concentrating light at their resonant frequencies are arranged quasi-randomly to provide both rich (with broadband Fourier components) and strong (with large intensities) Fourier spectra to satisfy the need of broadband antireflection, which can find promising applications in various areas including thin-film solar cells and imaging.

articleTitle: Bound States in the Continuum in Plasmonic Metasurfaces for Enhancing Graphene-Assisted Light Modulation
abstract: This letter reports bound states in the continuum dominated by magnetic-dipole resonances in plasmonic meta-surfaces. By simulation, high-quality perfect absorption with significant field enhancement is found for realizing graphene-assisted light modulation.

articleTitle: An FPGA-based Accelerator for Local Bundle Adjustment of Stereo Visual Odometry
abstract: This paper proposes an FPGA design and implementation of Local Bundle Adjustment (LBA) for Stereo Visual Odometry. In order to implement the LBA module on FPGA, binary Cauchy weight is designed. The LBA module is generated by Vivado HLS and implemented on the FPGA (XCZU3EG). Compared with the performance running on the FPGA and that on the Intel and ARM Processor, the LBA accelerator has achieved the highest speed which could speed up the process by 2.5 times than that on the Intel CPU, and 7.5 times than that on the ARM CPU. Based on improved LBA method on FPGA, the localization deviation is constrained within 10mm.

articleTitle: A Dual-Band Magneto-Electric Monopole Antenna Fed by a Self-Reconfigurable Waveguide
abstract: A dual-band magneto-electric (ME) monopole fed by a self-reconfigurable waveguide is proposed. By loading periodic structures with a stopband, the waveguide owns two operating bands supporting the single quasi TE<inf>10</inf> mode. The antenna is developed based on the combination of an open-ended self-reconfigurable waveguide and electric monopoles that separately operate in microwave and millimeter-wave bands. Stable radiation characteristics are achieved within the low-frequency band from 10.6 to 11.7 GHz and the high-frequency band from 30.9 to 41 GHz, respectively.

articleTitle: LMENet: A lightweight multiscale efficient convolutional neural network for image denoising
abstract: Various convolutional neural network (CNN) based image denoising methods have been proposed and achieved their attractive denoising performances in past decades. These methods benefit from carefully designed network structures via their increasing network depth and width. Since enlarged networks suffer from numerous parameters and cause heavy computational burden, their deployment application is limited on portable devices. To tackle this problem, we propose a lightweight multiscale efficient convolutional neural network (LMENet). It uses a set of cascaded residual networks (RNs) as its backbone network, where multiscale features are exported from these RNs. By fusing these features with a dual attention mechanism, denoised images are finally reconstructed. The experiments show that, compared with some state-of-the-art methods, our LMENet has a competitive performance for denoising in both additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) and real noise tests. More importantly, it has approximate one-eighth of the parameter size compared with the existing methods. It demonstrates the computational efficiency of the LMENet, while achieving similar PSNR results.

articleTitle: A File Sharing Method Using a Delay Tolerant Network in Daily Life
abstract: In this study, we will develop an application called DTNFileShare, which uses the delay tolerance network (DTN) for file sharing. Mobile terminals such as smartphones have become widely used. Mobile terminals can connect to networks by using communication infrastructure such as base stations and access points. However, information exchange using mobile terminals becomes difficult when the communication infrastructure cannot be used due to disasters or other reasons. Therefore, delay tolerant network exist as a technology to cope with these situations such as during a disaster. If DTN can be used not only in times of disaster but also in everyday life, files can be exchanged without depending on the communication infrastructure. However, there are two issues that need to be addressed when using DTN in everyday life. The first issue is that the timing of sending and receiving messages is not known by receiver and sender, respectively. The second issue is difficult to share the Endpoint ID (EID), which is the unique ID of the DTN, with others. DTNFileShare solves these two issues by integrating with Slack, a communication tool. With the implementation of the proposed system, EID can be shared at the touch of a button on the Slack application. In addition, notifications are sent to the Slack account when files are sent or received. These features make it comfortable to share files using DTN not only in times of disaster, but also in everyday life.

articleTitle: Pathogen-killing Polyethy lenimine-coated Nanodiamonds as Sprayable Disinfectants for Controlling Infectious Diseases
abstract: Nanodiamonds, with their unique physical properties and negligible toxicity, represent a new class of carbon-based nanomaterials in biomedical engineering field. Our work fosters the development of nanodiamond-based disinfectants that are potent in controlling infectious diseases.

articleTitle: Atomically Thin Nanomaterials-Enhanced Plasmonic Sensors Operating in Near-Infrared
abstract: In this paper, we investigated the sensing performance of a Goos-Hänchen shift-based surface plasmon resonance sensor enhanced by atomically thin phase change nanomaterials. The sensitivity enhancement based on this novel material has been demonstrated theoretically and experimentally in the visible and near-infrared regions (633 nm and 785 nm). With the phase change materials, the resonance dip was closer to zero and led to a higher optical phase related SPR sensitivity. Moreover, the excitation wavelength in the near-infrared region can significantly improve the Q factor of the SPR curves, which results in a higher sensing resolution. With the optimization of the excitation wavelength and the thickness of sensing substrate, approximately 100 times higher sensitivity has been obtained.

articleTitle: Learning phase retrieval without using real data
abstract: We propose a robust deep learning-based phase retrieval strategy with a high generalization potential for off-axis quantitative phase microscopy. Our strategy does not use real data and converges faster than end-to-end U-Net training approaches.

articleTitle: Analysis of capacity upgrading in L-band using power control strategy
abstract: To further increase the capacity of optical communication systems and networks with currently installed fibers, the L-band transmission needs to be exploited because the C-band spectral resource is going to be exhausted. From the perspective of network planning by operators, efficient estimation of increased capacity brought by added L-band channels is indispensable to evaluate the overall performance and cost. However, stimulated Raman scattering (SRS) arises for ultra-wideband transmission, which induces power transfer between low- and high-frequency channels. Moreover, the number of added L-band channels has an influence on the overall system performance through fiber nonlinearity. Above factors render the analysis of capacity upgrading beyond the mature C-band-only transmission a nontrivial task. In this letter, an analysis of capacity upgrading in L-band is provided using power control strategies including the local optimization global optimization (LOGO) algorithm and power offset and tilt control by OAs. It is found that with power control based on the LOGO results, not only quasi-linear capacity increase with the L-band channel number is provided, but higher overall capacity can be achieved compared with that with LOGO-only scheme.

articleTitle: High Refractive Index Meta-Unit Cells and Their Applications
abstract: Lenses are one of the good approaches applying to the design of fan-beam antennas due to the ease of producing wide operating bandwidths, directive radiation beam, and high capability in linear and circular polarization to the antennas. Conventional dielectric lens antennas usually suffer from limited range of the effective refraction index and then bulky size. Therefore, meta-unit cell with high refractive index is developed to design the lens with compact size and excellent performance. In this paper, our recently developed meta-unit cell with high refractive index is summarized and presented. Its electrical performances under different excitation case are analyzed. Two designs base on the presented meta-unit including the end-fire fan-beam radiation antenna and the low-profile wideband metasurface antenna are presented. The compact structure and good performance make the meta-unit cell appropriate for designing lens with compact size.

articleTitle: Combating high variance in Data-Scarce Implicit Hate Speech Classification
abstract: Hate speech classification has been a long-standing problem in natural language processing. However, even though there are numerous hate speech detection methods, they usually overlook a lot of hateful statements due to them being implicit in nature. Developing datasets to aid in the task of implicit hate speech classification comes with its own challenges; difficulties are nuances in language, varying definitions of what constitutes hate speech, and the labor-intensive process of annotating such data. This had led to a scarcity of data available to train and test such systems, which gives rise to high variance problems when parameter-heavy transformer-based models are used to address the problem. In this paper, we explore various optimization and regularization techniques and develop a novel RoBERTa-based model that achieves state-of-the-art performance.

articleTitle: Enhanced U-Net for Computer-aided Diagnosis with Cetacean Postmortem CT Scan
abstract: Postmortem computed tomography (PMCT) scan has long been used in the postmortem examination of cetaceans on Virtopsy to find out the cause of death such as diseases on internal organs.
